A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, Figures 1–2, Table 1, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison after matching relocated sections and renumbered theorems.

before.justification: v1 Section 7 and Figure 1 report original FedAvg experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10, comparing estimated generalization gaps with CMI bounds. Appendix H documents the experiments.

after.justification: v2 Section 6 and Figure 1 retain these original empirical results, with experimental details in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The superclient/supersample construction, model aggregation, and experimental FedAvg/CNN procedures are retained. Added discussion of truncation and regularization does not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST digit recognition and CIFAR-10 classification under the same non-IID client setting. No dataset, task, population, or evaluated test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the Fast-rate Bound and Square-root Bound comparisons against measured FedAvg generalization gaps. FedOpt is newly discussed in related work but is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The models, five local epochs, 300 communication rounds, sample-size/client-count sweeps, and zero-one evaluation loss remain unchanged. The added shard counts and sizes disclose an existing partitioning procedure rather than establish a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 1 retains the same analyses varying samples per client and participating-client counts. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix H retains three draws of supersamples and client-selection variables, 15 membership-variable draws per configuration, and 720 total FedAvg runs. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All four Figure 1 plots retain identical plotted results. The findings also remain unchanged: the fast-rate bound is tighter on MNIST, while the square-root bound is generally tighter on CIFAR-10. No result entries are added.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 in v1, renumbered 3.2 in v2, corrects the marginal-distribution definition by including U inside the conditional distribution averaged over U. The fast-rate theorem's explanation also changes the empirical-risk multiplier from C1C2−1 to C1C2. The bound inequalities and appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about two-level FL generalization, privacy connections, fast-rate and aggregation bounds, and non-vacuous empirical verification.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies the treatment of information terms as O(1) in rate statements, single-round aggregation scope, heavy-tailed-loss limitations, and why local CMI is not a direct heterogeneity measure. Appendix C adds possible gradient-regularization and feature-alignment interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 Section 6.1 newly specifies 200 label-sorted shards of 300 examples and random assignment of two shards per client. v1 described sharding and two-shard assignment without those counts. Appendix H's architectures, hyperparameters, estimation details, hardware, and code-source disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Reddi et al.'s adaptive federated optimization and two Wang–Mao works on hypothesis stability and SGD/SDE analysis. It also explains why comparison with Hellström–Durisi's meta-learning bounds requires accounting for local adaptation, while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 7, experimental setup/results become numbered subsections, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added. Local wording, affiliation, notation, and cross-reference edits accompany these changes; most prose and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The first-page layout and contribution-list formatting change, Figure 1 moves lower within page 8, and the homogeneous-case corollary becomes a displayed equation. Both figures and the notation table retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision and interpretability through the conditional-distribution correction and clearer qualifications concerning rates, single-round applicability, heterogeneity, and comparison with meta-learning. Added partition details improve documentation. The retained bounds, proofs, and experimental evidence limit the overall gain.
